uncited: This method classifies volumetric density data to render specific isosurfaces by mapping density values to color and opacity using a Gaussian function in logarithmic space.
It solves the problem of visualizing power-law density distributions (such as astrophysical gas) where linear scaling fails to provide smooth transitions.
It differs from linear transfer functions by operating on $\log_{10} n$, ensuring that the width of the rendered shell is constant in logarithmic density space rather than linear density space.
The transfer function $T(n)$ maps a density value $n$ to an intensity value (which is then applied to the RGB and $\alpha$ channels via amplitudes $h$).
This value is of the order of the grid cell size and must be tuned experimentally to scale the integration correctly.
The following Python-like pseudocode implements the transfer function evaluation for a single density value $n$ and a set of isosurface definitions.
